summary.title: Day 1: Parsing DMIDecode output
summary.one_liner: You learn how to write a line-by-line, indentation-aware state machine in Nim that parses dmidecode output into sections and properties.
takeaways: dmidecode output is made of meta lines, then sections that each start with a Handle line, a title line, and indented key/value properties.
Properties can have an optional list of indented items, so the parser must look at the next line's indentation to decide when to read a list.
A parser can be built as a small state machine (noOp, sectionName, readKeyValue, readList) driven by line content and indentation level.
Nim data structures for this are a Section ref object holding a Table of Property ref objects, each with a value and a seq of items.
summary.summary: This first post in the Nim Days series builds a parser for Linux dmidecode output, motivated by a past work need. It shows the output format (meta lines, Handle-started sections, indented properties and lists) and defines Nim types for Property and Section using ref objects and tables. The core parseDMI proc walks the lines with pairs and switches between parser states based on Handle lines, colons, empty lines, and indentation changes to fill the section tables.
